metric: ITU-R BT.2124-0 Delta E ITP from display-referred linear RGB in cd/m2
scope: These are provisional engineering gates for this fixture corpus, fixed before native measurements. They do not establish psychophysical invisibility or physical display qualification. Failed paths remain unqualified; new fixtures or revisions require new reviewed threshold profiles, never retrospective relaxation.

avif-8.reason: Synthetic PQ/HLG ramps and primary patches at 8 coded bits. Allow up to 3 Delta E ITP for 95% of each luminance region and 8 at any sample for quantization and native resampling near patch edges; errors are potentially visible and still require display review. A 0.1 nit absolute floor prevents quantized near-black noise dominating relative error. Eight-bit input is measured, never rejected by depth alone.

avif-10.reason: Synthetic 10-bit PQ/HLG ramps and patches retain four times the code precision of 8-bit inputs. A 1.5 Delta E ITP p95 gate and 4 maximum permit rounding and interpolation while rejecting changed transfer or primaries. The 0.025 nit floor applies only near black.

avif-12.reason: Synthetic 12-bit PQ/HLG samples should remain within roughly one just-noticeable difference for 95% of pixels in every luminance region. The 3 maximum allows isolated native interpolation/rounding differences; it cannot hide a changed transfer, clipping, or missing shadow region.

gainmap-sdr.reason: Authored 8-bit photographic SDR JPEG bases, compared after matched geometry and declared colour management at a nominal 100 nit SDR display. Native JPEG re-encoding may introduce small local error, but each region must keep mean Delta E ITP below 1 and p95 below 3. No broad whole-image average can compensate for damaged shadows.

gainmap-hdr.reason: Independently reconstructed gain-map JPEG HDR, using identical display boost and metadata conventions for source and result. Re-encoded base and map can each contribute error. A p95 Delta E ITP of 3 and maximum 8 still forbid broad exposure or grading changes. A decoder lacking the source gain-map model cannot supply evidence to this profile.

sdr-8.reason: Eight-bit SDR reference images at nominal 100 nits. Compare against the authored base or independently declared tone/gamut reference, never the unmodified HDR source. Regional p95 Delta E ITP of 3 accommodates quantization but does not approve the tone/gamut mapping itself; that needs the separate policy checks.

tone_map.reason: The synthetic chart contains neutral ramps, an exact 203 nit ordinary-white patch and 1000 nit peak. The accepted policy targets 90% nominal SDR signal, not 90% luminance. +/-0.025 signal allows codec rounding and a small perceptual grading tolerance. Below 100 nits, compare retained contrast to a linear exposure anchored at 203 nits -> sRGB 0.90. The broad 20% linear-light tolerance allows a mild shoulder; a black crush or peak-normalized dark image fails. Require at least 0.05 signal highlight headroom, no early 8-bit white clipping, no reversed neutral slope beyond one 8-bit code, and no >0.025 highlight signal jumps between the chart's closely spaced samples. Gamut mapping requires a separate, predeclared independent reference for chromatic probes.
